report.headline: Projected to take 23.2% of EuroLeague possessions, up from an 18.3% NBA usage rate that sat 0.34 sd below league average; the shooting-efficiency projection cannot be trusted for this transition.

projection.text: The model projects a EuroLeague usage rate of 23.2%, above the league's minutes-weighted average of 20.3% (sd 4.2%), with an 80% interval of 19.1%–27.3% and a 95% interval of 16.9%–29.5%; this projection beats the league-mean baseline (3.2% MAE vs 4.2%) so it carries real signal, even though the interval spans more than a full standard deviation on either side of the mean.

risks.text: The subject's NBA production was below league average on both tracked metrics (usage -0.34 sd, true shooting -0.37 sd), consistent with the broader NBA->EuroLeague mover cohort, which itself sits 0.31 sd below its own league average — the projection is conditional on a below-average-caliber mover, not a star.

The 80% usage interval (19.1%–27.3%) spans roughly two standard deviations of the EuroLeague usage distribution (sd 4.2%), meaning the model can rank this transition against others but cannot pin down the individual outcome closely.

The true-shooting projection is built on a model that loses to a trivial league-mean guess (4.5% vs 4.3% MAE) for this metric, so no efficiency conclusion should be drawn from the 55.5% figure or its interval.
Two full seasons elapsed between the source NBA season and the EuroLeague move, adding a gap of unknown developmental change not captured in the source-season statistics.

strengths.text: Projected usage of 23.2% clears the EuroLeague average of 20.3%, despite the subject's NBA usage sitting below the NBA average (-0.34 sd), and exceeds both the standing-preservation baseline of 18.9% and the naive 0.75x folk-rule estimate of 13.8%.

Source-season assist rate of 16.7% (3.816 assists per 75 possessions) indicates a playmaking component to the profile that fed into a usage-rate model whose slope for this pathway preserves 97.7% of a player's standing above their league.

uncertainty.text: The true-shooting projection of 55.5% (80% interval 48.9%–62.0%, 95% interval 45.5%–65.5%) should not be treated as informative: the model's out-of-fold error (4.5%) is worse than simply guessing the EuroLeague average (4.3%), so this number adds nothing beyond the league mean of 56.1%.
